title: Harlem Globetrotters: Rivalry Tour Coming to The Aud
content: Get ready for an unforgettable family experience as the world-famous Harlem Globetrotters bring their all-new Rivalry Tour to The Aud on Thursday, January 28, 2027.
Perfect for fans of all ages, the Harlem Globetrotters continue their tradition of combining incredible basketball skills, comedy and entertainment into a one-of-a-kind live event.

The rivalry is theirs. The thrill is yours. For tickets and event information, visit The Harlem Globetrotters | Kitchener Live .

title: Cowan Recreation Centre grand opening to feature debut of Indigenous art installation focused on what connects us, by Jackie Traverse
content: Installation of GIDINAWENDIMIN , a featured Indigenous public artwork at the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park, is now complete ahead of the facility's grand opening on November 14, 2026 .

Created by renowned Indigenous artist Jackie Traverse, GIDINAWENDIMIN , an Anishinaabe word meaning "we are all related," is a large-scale mosaic installed in the aquatics centre. Spanning 95 square metres and made with more than 200,000 glass tiles, GIDINAWENDIMIN  features four women interwoven with flowing lines of water. The piece is a celebration of the cultural and spiritual relationship between women and water while exploring themes of kinship, resilience and connection.

“Thousands of residents will walk through the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park each year, and  GIDINAWENDIMIN  will help shape their experience of the space,” said Kitchener Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. “It's a work that speaks to connection, community and our relationship with the water , and I'm proud it will be part of a facility that will bring Kitchener community members together every day .”

Jackie Traverse is an Anishinaabe artist from Lake St. Martin First Nation whose multidisciplinary practice is rooted in her culture, community and lived experience. Working across painting, sculpture, mixed media and moving image, Traverse creates bold, deeply personal work that explores Indigenous identity, womanhood, resilience and social justice. Central to her practice are the strength and voices of Indigenous women, the transmission of knowledge across generations, and our relationships with land and water.

GIDINAWENDIMIN was created in collaboration with Highness Global Inc., the art agency and design firm that supports Jackie Traverse in bringing her large-scale projects to life, from creative development through fabrication and installation.

“Water connects all of us. In Anishinaabe teachings, women carry the water teachings and have a sacred responsibility to protect and care for nibi,” said Jackie Traverse, Artist. “ GIDINAWENDIMIN  speaks to that connection, to the strength carried through generations of women, and to our responsibility to care for the water and one another. I hope people experience that sense of connection when they spend time with the work.”

Designed to promote connection, accessibility and inclusion, the Cowan Recreation Centre aims to be a space where everyone can connect, compete and belong. GIDINAWENDIMIN  reinforces that vision, celebrating the relationships that connect people to one another, to water and to community.

“It was an honour to help select this important piece of community art, ” shared Ward 8 Councillor Margaret Johnston. “ The artist’s work not only complements the design of the aquatics centre, but it also helps tell the story of a facility built to bring people together and creates a welcoming space where visitors will see themselves and their relationships reflected around them."

Residents will be able to view GIDINAWENDIMIN  for the first time during the Cowan Recreation Centre's grand opening celebration on Saturday, November 14. The free community event will include an official ribbon-cutting ceremony, free public swims, sport activities, family-friendly entertainment and activities throughout the day.
As visitors explore the new facility this fall, GIDINAWENDIMIN  will serve as a lasting reminder of the relationships that connect people, water and community.

To stay up-to-date on grand opening details, future programming and amenities, and more, visit the City's newly launched RBJ Schlegel Park webpage which includes detailed information about the Cowan Recreation Centre – Kitchener.ca/RBJSchlegelPark
QUICK FACTS
About the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park

The City of Kitchener received funding from the Government of Canada and the Province of Ontario through the Investing in Canada Infrastructure Program (ICIP) Community, Culture and Recreation Stream to support the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park.
The Cowan Recreation Centre is one of the largest and most sustainable municipally owned recreation centres in Canada.

The centre offers diverse recreation opportunities with a quad gymnasium, FIFA-sized indoor turf field, cricket practice nets, competition and leisure pools, and an indoor walking track, supporting sports and activities ranging from basketball and soccer to pickleball, badminton and swimming.

The facility is the most accessible building ever constructed by the City of Kitchener, designed to meet the City's highest accessibility standards and shaped through input from accessibility advocates. It features pool ramps, wider pathways, tactile wayfinding elements and accessible viewing areas.
Built to host provincial and national competitions, tournaments and major events, the centre will help showcase Kitchener, support local businesses and generate economic benefits for the community.
City of Kitchener’s 1% policy

GIDINAWENDIMIN was funded through the City of Kitchener’s1% for Public Art Policy, which allocates one per cent of eligible civic construction budgets to public art projects. The policy is intended to create better quality of life and increased social cohesion for residents, local artists and visitors; good urban design; broad community involvement and connection; and increased potential for economic development and public access to the arts.
For more information:  Corporate Communications and Marketing City of Kitchener media@kitchener.ca

title: Working together to protect jobs: Mayor Berry Vrbanovic and Senator Sandra Pupatello convene procurement and defence-sector leaders to support local businesses
content: The City of Kitchener, Office of Mayor and Council and Senator Sandra Pupatello are inviting local businesses to register for three free sessions at Kitchener City Hall on October 13 and 14.

Businesses from across Kitchener-Waterloo-Cambridge and surrounding areas can register for the sessions to learn how to compete for public-sector contracts and explore opportunities to enter or grow within Canada’s defence sector. Attendees will have the opportunity to speak directly with federal and provincial procurement officials, Canada's Defence Investments Agency and companies such as Boeing Canada, Bombardier and Honeywell Aerospace, helping them pursue new customers, contracts and markets.

“Kitchener is home to manufacturers, technology companies, health-sector innovators and entrepreneurs with the expertise to compete for major government and defence opportunities,” said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. “By bringing procurement officials and industry leaders directly to Kitchener, we are helping local businesses build new relationships, reach new customers and create opportunities that support local jobs. This is one of the practical ways we are delivering on our plan to support local and Build Canada Strong by building a stronger, more resilient economy.”

During the October 13, Buy Canada – Buy Ontario sessions, representatives from Public Services and Procurement Canada and Supply Ontario will explain what governments purchase, how businesses can register as suppliers and where to find upcoming opportunities. The construction-focused session will also include Infrastructure Ontario and highlight opportunities in construction, heavy construction and infrastructure.

The Defence Shift will help companies assess whether their products, services or expertise could meet the needs of Canada’s defence supply chain. Businesses will hear from federal defence officials and connect directly with defence prime contractors and Tier 1 suppliers. The session is designed to help local companies diversify their customer base and pursue opportunities beyond their traditional markets.

"Companies not found in the country's capital regions may not consider the opportunities they have to sell their goods and services to government -provincial and federal governments are committed through Buy Canada and Buy Ontario policies,” said The Honourable Sandra Pupatello, Senator. “Now, we have to give our companies the details they need to respond.  That's what this day is about in Kitchener. Great companies finding new business opportunities."
Session details and registration
All sessions are free and take place at Kitchener City Hall, 200 King St. W. Space is limited and guests are asked to register.
Buy Canada – Buy Ontario Information Session for Construction Companies. Register here
Buy Canada – Buy Ontario Information Session, open to businesses of all sizes and sectors. Please send one representative per company. Register here
The Defence Shift. Register here

These sessions are part of Kitchener’s Plan to Support Local and Protect Jobs , which outlines practical actions to strengthen local businesses, open doors to new markets and build a more resilient economy. Through the plan, the City is using its purchasing power, partnerships and influence to create opportunities for local businesses and help protect local jobs.
About Senator Pupatello

Sandra Pupatello is a former provincial politician, businesswoman and advocate for Ontario’s economic growth, with more than 30 years of experience in public service, corporate leadership, and community engagement. First elected as MPP for Windsor West in 1995, she served in several cabinet positions, including Minister of Economic Development and Trade, Education, Women’s Issues, and Community and Social Services. She also served as Vice-Chair of Ontario’s Treasury Board and led trade delegations around the world.

Prior to entering politics, Ms. Pupatello worked and volunteered in the non-profit sector. She later founded Canadian International Avenues Ltd., a management consulting firm, and has served on several corporate and public-sector boards, including as Chair of Hydro One and Chair of the Toronto Port Authority.
She currently serves on the Board of Martinrea International and the Saint Elizabeth Foundation. During the COVID-19 pandemic, she co-founded and co-chaired Reshoring Canada.

Ms. Pupatello has received numerous awards and distinctions, including recognition among WXN’s Top 100 Most Powerful Women in Canada and the Windsor-Essex Chamber of Commerce Lifetime Achievement Award.
She holds a Bachelor of Arts (Honours) and an Honorary Doctor of Laws from the University of Windsor, as well as a Corporate Director Certificate from the University of Toronto.
About Mayor Vrbanovic

Mayor Berry Vrbanovic was elected in 2014 as the 68th Mayor of the City of Kitchener since its founding as the Village of Berlin in 1854. As Mayor, he also sits as a member of the council of the Regional Municipality of Waterloo. Prior to being elected Mayor, he served as a City Councillor from 1994-2014.

Born in Zagreb, Croatia, Mayor Vrbanovic moved to Canada as a young child. He is a graduate of the Waterloo Catholic District School Board, Wilfrid Laurier University and the Bloomberg Harvard City Leadership Initiative. Coming from an immigrant family himself, he understands the challenges and issues facing the thousands of Canadians who have made Kitchener their new home.

Mayor Vrbanovic was recently re-elected Co-President of United Cities and Local Governments and in April 2026 was appointed as the Chair of the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) Green Municipal Fund Council.  He also serves on FCM committees including its Big Cities Mayors’ Caucus, as well as with the Association of Municipalities of Ontario Big City Mayors.
For more information: Corporate Communications and Marketing City of Kitchener Media@kitchener.ca

title: Applications now open for 2027 Artist in Residence program
content: The City of Kitchener is inviting artists to apply for the 2027 Artist in Residence program . This program – the oldest of its kind in Canada – supports artistic innovation and excellence and encourages artists to develop their practice or interests as they engage and collaborate with the community. Each year, a new artist holds the position, showcasing the diversity of our region.

The 2027 Artist in Residence program will bring an artist into the Lancaster West community to work with residents and explore what makes the neighbourhood unique. Through hands-on workshops and creative activities connected to the Lancaster West parks, residents will be invited to share stories, ideas and experiences related to community identity and sense of place. The artist will collect and document these themes through a variety of creative formats, such as writing, photography, artwork or digital media. The insights gathered during the residency will help shape a future public art project planned for the Lancaster West Park Network.

This is a part-time, six-month position where the artist will have the flexibility to plan a time commitment that reflects the needs of their proposal.  Artists must live, work or have an ongoing connection or affiliation with Kitchener or Waterloo Region. The selected artist will have the opportunity to collaborate with the community and members of the local arts sector as they advance their artistic practice. The City encourages applications from all artists and highly encourages applications from individuals from equity-deserving groups.
Interested artists have until 5:00 p.m. on December 3, 2026 to apply. Applications can be submitted through the City’s online form , email, in-person delivery or mail.
The City will be holding two optional information sessions to answer questions about the 2027 residency. Sessions will be held at Kitchener City Hall, 200 King Street West, on:
The Conestoga Room on the ground floor of Kitchener City Hall
The Schmalz Room, on the second floor of Kitchener City Hall

No registration is required. Interested individuals only need to come to one session. You do not need to attend a session to submit a proposal. If you have any questions or require any accessible accommodation, please send us an email or call 519-783-8302.
To learn more about the City’s Artist in Residence program, submission requirements and for any questions about the opportunity, visit www.kitchener.ca/AIRProposals .

title: Fire Prevention Week highlights simple steps to prevent fires and save lives
content: Fire Prevention Week is October 4 to 10 and Kitchener Fire is encouraging residents to make fire safety part of their everyday routine. By practicing these simple tips, you can keep yourself, your family and the community safe.
Smoke and carbon monoxide alarms save lives.
Distracted or unattended cooking is the leading cause of home fires in Canada.
Lithium-ion battery safety protects your devices and yourself.
Having a home fire escape plan keeps you prepared.
To learn more about fire safety and emergency preparedness, visit KitchenerFire.ca

title: Grab lunch for a cause at Kitchener's annual Grillefest
content: The City of Kitchener is inviting the community to enjoy lunch for a good cause at Grillefest on Friday, October 9 from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. in front of Kitchener City Hall. For more than 20 years, the City's annual Oktoberfest fundraiser has brought together residents, City staff and members of Council to share a meal, celebrate community spirit and support the Food Bank of Waterloo Region .

Each year, Grillefest serves more than 1,500 sausage lunches, helping raise funds and collect food donations that support local families experiencing food insecurity. In 2025, the event raised nearly $5,000 for the Food Bank. Combined with non-perishable food donations, this supported over 9,800 meals for local families in need. The event has become a longstanding community tradition that demonstrates the generosity of Kitchener residents and the collective impact of coming together for a common cause.

From 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. on Friday, October 9 in front of Kitchener City Hall, councillors and City staff will cook up traditional sausages served to you on a fresh bun and accompanied by a cold drink and cookies, all for only a minimum donation of $5. All proceeds from the lunch support the Food Bank of Waterloo Region.
Community members are also encouraged to bring dry and canned food donations, which can be dropped off at the event or in advance at the donation box located in the City Hall Rotunda.
The event would not be possible without the support of our sponsors: Piller's Fine Foods, Grainharvest Breadhouse, Zehr's and Costco Kitchener.
More information is available at Kitchener.ca/Grillefest

title: Your city. Your voice. Your vote on October 26.
content: The 2026 municipal and school board election is your opportunity to help shape the future of Kitchener. The decisions made by local elected officials affect everyday services, including roads, parks, community programs, Kitchener Fire Department, property taxes and more.
Take a few minutes today to make sure you're ready to vote on October 26, 2026.

You must be a Canadian citizen, at least 18 years old on October 26, 2026, and live in Kitchener, own or rent property in Kitchener, or be the spouse of an owner or tenant. Eligible voters must also not be prohibited from voting.
Check that you're on the voter list and that your name, address and school board information are up to date.

If you need to update your information, you can do this at City Hall, or you can also update your voter information at a voting location during advance voting or on Election Day. Allow extra time if you choose to amend/add yourself to the voters list when you go to vote..
Not on the voters list? You can still vote if you're eligible. Bring identification showing your name and current address.
Review the list of candidates and do your research to learn where they stand on the issues that matter most to you.
The City of Kitchener is providing a range of vote opportunities to remove barriers for residents so they can practice their democratic rights safely and easily.
The City is committed to making​​ voting accessible for everyone.

During Advance voting, Kitchener voters can “vote anywhere” at a number of facilities across the city including two Shop and Vote locations, the Kitchener Market and Fairview Park Mall. We’re taking the vote to where people are.

On voting day we provide accessible voting locations in every​ ward, offer different voting options and supply accessibility tools at voting locations. Voters may also bring their own devices to help mark their ballot. Learn more below about how we make voting accessible during municipal elections.
Kitchener voters looking for a convenient and accessible new voting method are encouraged to try drive thru voting.

Kitchener voters will remain in their vehicles until prompted to drive into the tent location. After turning off their vehicles, an election official will conduct the voting service at the vehicle window(s). Electors will be given a ballot in a privacy screen so that other people that may be in the vehicle cannot see their selections. Marked ballots will be collected back through the window(s) and cast into the tabulator. Once cast, the vehicle will exit the tent location.
Drive thru voting operates like the COVID-vaccination drive thru process.

It’s a convenient method for electors that may have mobility challenges, limits exposure for individuals who may have health considerations, and reduces the need to unbuckle and remove young children and seniors.
The dates and times that drive thru is being offered can be found on the Where to vote page .

Kitchener voters who cannot leave their homes due to illness, injury or disability may request a home vote visit where election workers will bring a ballot to them. The voter's caregiver(s) who are eligible voters may also vote during the home visit. Home votes will only take place within the boundaries of the City of Kitchener.

Home voting will be available for a limited number of appointments, between 9:30 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. on weekdays from Thursday, October 8 until Tuesday, October 20 (not including Thanksgiving, Monday, October 12).
Requests for home visits will be accepted starting on September 28.
You can request a home visit by;
email at election@kitchener.ca .
Voters are encouraged to book their own appointment as soon as possible.
The deadline to request a home voting appointment is at 4:30 p.m. on Monday, October 19, 2026.

If Kitchener voters are away for all the Advance Voting or Voting Day locations, they may appoint another eligible voter as a proxy to vote on their behalf.  To appoint a voting proxy, the voter and their proxy must complete two copies with original signatures of the Appointment for Voting Proxy form.

The voter being appointed as a proxy must then book an appointment at Kitchener City Hall. They must bring with them the two completed forms, their own ID, and a copy of ID for the voter who is appointing them that proves the voter’s residency and signature.

Voters requiring assistance can take advantage of a number of accessibility enhancements including; accessible ballot marking devices at advance and designated election day locations, magnifying sheets, translation through the city’s multi-language service interpretation service and support from service animals and support persons.
View the City’s Election Accessibility Plan for more details including other initiatives designed to make elections accessible.
Visit KitchenerVotes.ca for everything you need to know about voter eligibility, candidate information, voting options and locations and accessibility planning.
Make your mark. Local matters.

title: City of Kitchener celebrates grand reopening of Meadowlane Park and new stormwater management pond
content: Kitchener, ON - The City of Kitchener celebrated the completion and grand reopening of the Meadowlane Park and a new stormwater management pond on Saturday, marking a significant investment in climate resilience, environmental stewardship and community infrastructure.

Meadowlane Park has been transformed through a project designed to reduce flood risk, enhance water quality and strengthen climate resilience within the Sandrock Creek watershed and downstream neighbourhoods.

The project was identified through the City of Kitchener’s 2016 Integrated Stormwater Master Plan as an opportunity to improve stormwater management while enhancing green space. The new pond will help manage stormwater runoff before it enters local waterways, reducing impacts on the environment and supporting the community’s long-term resilience to more frequent and intense storms.

The project was supported through funding from all orders of government, including $2.143 million from the Government of Canada’s Disaster Mitigation and Adaptation Fund, $3 million from the Province of Ontario through the Building Faster Fund, and $178,500 from the Federation of Canadian Municipalities through the Growing Canada’s Community Canopies program , alongside contributions from the City of Kitchener.

“This project demonstrates the power of partnership. Meadowlane Park is a great example of what can be accomplished when all orders of government work together to invest in communities,” said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. “On behalf of the City of Kitchener, I want to thank the Government of Canada, the Province of Ontario and the Federation of Canadian Municipalities for their support in bringing this important project to life. Together, we’re creating greener, more resilient public spaces that will benefit residents today and for generations to come.”

“Meadowlane Park has always been an important gathering place for residents in the Forest Heights neighbourhood, and I’m proud to see it transformed in a way that preserves its community character while delivering significant environmental benefits,” said Bil Ioannidis, Ward 7 Councillor. “This project reflects the feedback we heard from residents and demonstrates how community priorities and environmental stewardship can come together to create a stronger, more resilient neighbourhood.”

The project reflects extensive community engagement. Several residents volunteered significant time as members of the Meadowlane Park Community Resource Group, playing an active role in shaping both the engagement process and park design. Their contributions, alongside feedback gathered through six community engagement events, helped inform the final design and preserve valued community features while meeting the project's environmental and infrastructure objectives.

In addition to improving stormwater management, the project includes environmental enhancements that support a healthier and more resilient urban ecosystem, including new trees and naturalized areas supported through funding from the Federation of Canadian Municipalities’ Growing Canada’s Community Canopies program, as well as upgraded trails, new pond-side pathways and seating areas for residents to enjoy.
Quotes:

“By investing in stormwater management infrastructure, like Kitchener’s new stormwater management pond, the Government of Canada is taking action to better protect Canadians from the impacts of severe weather events and storms. The stormwater management pond will reduce the risk of flooding in streets and neighbourhoods near Meadowlane Park.”

– Tim Louis, Parliamentary Secretary to the President of the King’s Privy Council for Canada and Minister responsible for Canada-U.S. Trade, Intergovernmental Affairs, Internal Trade and One Canadian Economy and Member of Parliament for Kitchener—Conestoga

“Our government is proud to support partners like the City of Kitchener with the tools they need to make infrastructure investments that keep them strong, resilient, and ready for the future. Through the Building Faster Fund, we’re pleased to see municipalities deliver projects like Meadowlane Park that protect neighbourhoods from extreme weather, strengthen local infrastructure, and create vibrant public spaces for families to enjoy for years to come.”
– Rob Flack, Ontario’s Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing.

“FCM is proud to support the City of Kitchener’s transformative tree-planting project. Through the Growing Canada’s Community Canopies initiative and with the support of the Government of Canada, we’re helping municipalities of every size get the right trees in the ground in the right places, creating cooler streets, cleaner air, and healthier neighbourhoods for decades to come.”
– Tim Tierney, President, Federation of Canadian Municipalities
About FCM’s Green Municipal Fund

FCM’s Green Municipal Fund (GMF) is a globally unique organization providing funding and education to municipalities to help them both reach net-zero and build resilient communities, while also delivering economic and social benefits such as jobs, housing and infrastructure. Since inception in 2000, it has helped reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 3.02 million tonnes, funded nearly 60,000 person-years of employment and contributed $5.6 billion to the national GDP via the more than 2,850 approved projects. GMF manages approximately $2.4 billion in programs funded by the Government of Canada.

The Green Municipal Fund’s Growing Canada’s Community Canopies is a $291M initiative, ending in 2031, funded by the Government of Canada and delivered by the FCM. Capacity building is enabled through a partnership with Tree Canada.

title: City of Kitchener invites community to share local stories as they put a Spotlight on Sport at the Cowan Recreation Centre
content: The City of Kitchener is inviting residents to help put a spotlight on local sports by celebrating the people and organizations who make Kitchener a vibrant, active and connected community through a permanent community showcase in the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park.

When the facility opens on November 14, visitors will discover Spotlight on Sport , a community storytelling space located in the main corridor beside the Cowan Fieldhouse. Featuring four large digital displays, photos, memorabilia, athlete and team profiles, and rotating community-submitted stories, Spotlight on Sport will celebrate the athletes, coaches, officials, volunteers, teams, organizations, and community champions who have helped shape sport and recreation in Kitchener. Through featured profiles and community submissions, the exhibit showcases achievements, inspires participation, and highlights the many ways sport helps communities connect.

"Sport is about much more than competition. It creates connections, builds confidence, brings people together in what often become lifelong friendships, and helps create a sense of belonging in our community," said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. "Every day, athletes, coaches, volunteers, officials, and organizations across Kitchener make a positive difference in the lives of others, here in Kitchener and often beyond our community’s borders. The Spotlight on Sport at the Cowan Recreation Centre gives us an opportunity to celebrate their contributions, preserve their stories, and inspire future generations to get involved."

From grassroots programs and neighbourhood leagues to provincial, national, and international achievements, Spotlight on Sport will showcase the many ways sport strengthens our community and creates meaningful connections. The exhibit will celebrate not only athletic success, but also leadership, inclusion, mentorship, volunteerism, and community building. The inaugural exhibit will feature Kitchener-born soccer players, Leticia Skeete and Markus Cimermancic, as well as former professional volleyball player Sarah Pavan and national men’s wheelchair basketball veteran, Tyler Miller.

"Every community has inspiring sport stories that deserve to be told," said Mark McGinley, Manager, Cowan Recreation Centre. "Whether it's a volunteer who has dedicated decades to local programs, a team that brought a community together, or a young athlete who inspires others through their commitment and determination, Spotlight on Sport will help share and celebrate those stories."

Do you know someone who is making a difference through sport in Kitchener? Share your stories or nominate an individual, team, or organization whose dedication, leadership, and accomplishments deserve recognition.
Learn more about Spotlight on Sport and submit a story or nomination at Kitchener.ca/spotlightonsport
